ledger.x: 926: the county first appears as a vassal state of France.
1279: Eleanor of Castile, wife of Edward I, inherits Ponthieu, which passes to the English crown.
1294: Philip IV confiscates Ponthieu and the French crown holds it.
1303: Ponthieu reverts to the English crown after the Gascon War.
1360: the Treaty of Brétigny puts Ponthieu under English control.
April 1369: Charles V of France conquers Ponthieu and the French crown holds it again.
20/21 September 1435: the Treaty of Arras gives Ponthieu to the Duke of Burgundy.
1477: Louis XI reconquers Ponthieu from Burgundy and the county becomes crown land.
1477: Ponthieu ceases to be a separate county and becomes crown land.

wars.name: Gascon War (Ponthieu)
wars.outcome: Philip IV confiscated Ponthieu in 1294; it reverted to Edward after the war (1294-1303).

certainty.note: A small county with no boundary record on the page; the 35 km disc round Abbeville is my reading.
